blocks.text: ECMAScript 2019
New Features in JavaScript 2019

rows: Removes whitespace from the start of a string
Removes whitespace from the end of a string
Creates an object from key/value pairs
Allows to omit the catch parameter if it is not needed
Creates a new array by flattening a nested array
Maps all array elements and creates a new array by flattening the array
Browsers must now use a stable sorting algorithm
Strings with UTF-8 code points now convert safely
Line and paragraph separators (\u2028 and \u2029) are now allowed in strings
Now returns source code including comments and spaces and syntax details

blocks.text: Browser Support
ECMAScript 2019 is supported in all modern browsers since January 2020:
JavaScript String trimStart()
ES2019 added the String method trimStart() to JavaScript.
The trimStart() method works like trim(), but removes whitespace only from the start of a string.

let text1 = "     Hello World!     ";

let text2 = text1.trimStart();
blocks.caption: Example

blocks.text: JavaScript String trimEnd()
ES2019 added the String method trimEnd() to JavaScript.
The trimEnd() method works like trim(), but removes whitespace only from the end of a string.

let text1 = "     Hello World!     ";

let text2 = text1.trimEnd();
blocks.caption: Example

blocks.text: JavaScript Object fromEntries()
ES2019 added the Object method fromEntries() to JavaScript.
The fromEntries() method creates an object from iterable key / value pairs.

blocks.text: JavaScript Array flat()
ES2019 added the Array flat() method to JavaScript.
The flat() method creates a new array by flattening a nested array.

const myArr = [[1,2],[3,4],[5,6]];

const newArr = myArr.flat();
blocks.caption: Example

blocks.text: JavaScript Array flatMap()
ES2019 added the Array flatMap() method to JavaScript.

The flatMap() method first maps all elements of an array
and then creates a new array by flattening the array.

const myArr = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6];

const newArr = myArr.flatMap(x => [x, x * 10]);
blocks.caption: Example

blocks.text: Stable Array sort()

Revised JSON.stringify()
ES2019 revised the JSON stringify() method.
Before 2019, JSON could not stringify character encoded with \.
let text = JSON.stringify("\u26D4");
blocks.caption: Example

blocks.text:
Before ES2019, using JSON.stringify()JSON on UTF-8 code points (U+D800 to U+DFFF)
returned broken Unicode characters like ���.

After this revision, strings with UTF-8 code points convert safely with JSON.stringify(),
and back to the original using JSON.parse().
Separator Symbols
Line separators and paragraph separator symbols (\u2028 and \u2029) are now allowed in string literals.
Before 2019, these were treated as line terminators and resulted in error exceptions:

// This is valid in ES2019:

let text = "\u2028";
blocks.caption: Example

blocks.text: Now, JavaScript and JSON have equal rules.
Before ES2019:
text = JSON.parse('"\u2028"') would parse to ''.
text = '"\u2028"' would give syntax error.
Revised Function toString()
ES2019 revised the Function toString() method.
The toString() method returns a string representing the source code of a function.

From 2019, toString() must return the source code of the function including comments,
spaces, and syntax details.

Before 2019, different browsers returned different variants of the function (like without comments and spaces).
From 2019 the function should be returned exactly as it is written.
